arxiv-2405-15428.title: Enhancing Pollinator Conservation towards Agriculture 4.0: Monitoring of Bees through Object Recognition
arxiv-2405-15428.creator: Ajay John Alex, Chloe M. Barnes, Pedro Machado, Isibor Ihianle, Gábor Markó, Martin Bencsik, Jordan J. Bird
arxiv-2405-15428.description: Abstract In an era of rapid climate change and its adverse effects on food production, technological intervention to monitor pollinator conservation is of paramount importance for environmental monitoring and conservation for global food security. The survival of the human species depends on the conservation of pollinators.

arxiv-2406-11140.title: Computing the Frequency Response of Biochemical Networks: A Python module
arxiv-2406-11140.creator: Herbert M. Sauro
arxiv-2406-11140.description: Abstract In this paper, a set of Python methods is described that can be used to compute the frequency response of an arbitrary biochemical network given any input and output. Models can be provided in standard SBML or Antimony format.

arxiv-2408-04935.title: Qualitatively altered driven Dicke superradiance in extended systems due to infinitesimal perturbations
arxiv-2408-04935.creator: Wenqi Tong, F. Robicheaux
arxiv-2408-04935.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Wenqi Tong, F. Robicheaux. The driven Dicke model, with interesting quantum phases induced by parameterized driving, has been intensively studied in cavities, where permutation symmetry applies due to the atoms’ equal coupling to the field and identical interaction. As a result, the system, with proper initialization, can remain in a highly symmetric subset of the state space, where the photon emission of each atom constructively interferes with each other, leading to superradiance at steady state.

arxiv-2409-15820.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning Achieve Rapid Task Adaption Via Alternating Attention Head Activation Patterns
arxiv-2409-15820.creator: Yang Zhao, Li Du, Xiao Ding, Kai Xiong, Ting Liu and Bing Qin
arxiv-2409-15820.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yang Zhao, Li Du, Xiao Ding, Kai Xiong, Ting Liu and Bing Qin. LLMs’ performance on complex tasks is still unsatisfactory. A key issue is that presently LLMs learn in a data-driven schema, while the instructions about these complex tasks are both scarce and hard to collect or construct. On the contrary, a prominent phenomenon is that LLMs can learn rather fast on simpler tasks with adequate prior knowledge captured during pretraining stage.

arxiv-2411-03392.title: Inverse See-Saw Mechanism with 𝐒 3 \mathbf{S}_{3} flavor symmetry
arxiv-2411-03392.creator: Juan Carlos Gómez-Izquierdo, Catalina Espinoza, Lucia E. Gutiérrez Luna, Myriam Mondragón
arxiv-2411-03392.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Juan Carlos Gómez-Izquierdo, Catalina Espinoza, Lucia E. Gutiérrez Luna, Myriam Mondragón. The current neutrino experiments provide an opportunity for testing the inverse see-saw mechanism through charged lepton flavor violating processes and neutrinoless double beta decay. Motivated by this, in this paper we study the 𝐒 3 ⊗ 𝐙 2 \mathbf{S}_{3}\otimes\mathbf{Z}_{2} discrete symmetry in the B − L B-L gauge model where the active light neutrino mass matrix comes from the aforementioned mechanism.

arxiv-2504-13556.title: On a stochastic epidemic SIR model with non homogenous population: a toy model for HIV
arxiv-2504-13556.description: Abstract In this paper we generalise a simple discrete time stochastic SIR type model defined by Tuckwell and Williams. The SIR model by Tuckwell and Williams assumes a homogeneous population, a fixed infectious period, and a strict transition from susceptible to infected to recovered.

pmc-11442341.title: Management of Rapid Atrial Fibrillation Using Stellate Ganglion Blockade
pmc-11442341.creator: Jacob Groenendyk, Ari Mandler, Danny Luan, Erden Goljo, Tiffany Tedore, Jim W Cheung, Steven M Markowitz
pmc-11442341.description: BackgroundStellate ganglion blockade has been demonstrated as an efficacious treatment for refractory ventricular tachyarrhythmias. There are no published reports of the use of this technique in management of rapid atrial arrhythmia.Case SummaryA 73-year-old woman presented to our institution in rapid atrial fibrillation and cardiogenic shock. She was intubated for airway protection and underwent successful electrical cardioversion.

pmc-11493884.title: Adopting Interventional Glaucoma Via Sustained-Release Therapies: The Wide-Ranging Impact of Procedural Pharmaceuticals in Ophthalmology
pmc-11493884.creator: Arkadiy Yadgarov, Lorraine Provencher, Brian Shafer, Christine Funke
pmc-11493884.description: Topical medical therapy is the most common approach to the treatment of many ocular conditions. While effective, topical therapy has numerous important limitations. Eye drops can have unpleasant or even dangerous side effects, are often difficult to self-administer, and the application of multiple drops per day, possibly from multiple different bottles, can be burdensome.

pmc-11503411.title: Polyphenols Regulate the Activity of Endocrine-Disrupting Chemicals, Having Both Positive and Negative Effects
pmc-11503411.creator: Eleonora Leti Maggio, Carlotta Zucca, Martina Grande, Raffaele Carrano, Antonio Infante, Riccardo Bei, Valeria Lucarini, Fernando De Maio, Chiara Focaccetti, Camilla Palumbo, Stefano Marini, Elisabetta Ferretti, Loredana Cifaldi, Laura Masuelli, Monica Benvenuto, Roberto Bei
pmc-11503411.description: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) are chemical substances that can interfere with any hormone action. They are categorized according to origin and use, such as industrial chemicals like polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and polybrominated biphenyls (PBBs), plastics like bisphenol A (BPA), plasticizers like phthalates, pesticides like dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (DDT), fungicides like vinclozolin, and pharmaceuticals like diethylstilbestrol (DES).

pmc-11600226.title: Use of Multiplex Molecular Panels to Diagnose Urinary Tract Infection in Older Adults
pmc-11600226.creator: Kelly M. Hatfield, Sarah Kabbani, Isaac See, Dustin W. Currie, Christine Kim, Kara Jacobs Slifka, Shelley S. Magill, Lauri A. Hicks, L. Clifford McDonald, John Jernigan, Sujan C. Reddy, Joseph D. Lutgring
pmc-11600226.description: Key PointsQuestionHow frequently are multiplex molecular syndromic panels used to diagnose urinary tract infection (UTI) among older Medicare beneficiaries?FindingsIn this cohort study of older adults, Medicare fee-for-service claims for multiplex testing with a primary diagnosis of UTI increased from 2 to 148 claims per 10 000 beneficiaries annually between 2016 and 2023.

pmc-13286473.creator: Shigeki Yamamoto, Norio Akuta, Tetsuya Hosaka, Yasuka Eriksson, Shunya Goto, Yasue Takeuchi, Hitomi Sezaki, Satoshi Saitoh, Mariko Kobayashi, Hiromitsu Kumada, Fumitaka Suzuki
pmc-13286473.description: IntroductionAtezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a standard first-line therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, a proportion of patients develop early progressive disease (PD).
